answer: At each dawn the network issues a crystal‑signed credential tied to a unique knoll‑indexed hardware enclave; agents must bond a stake that is cryptographically locked to that enclave. When a new identity appears, peers challenge it by requesting a zero‑knowledge proof of enclave ownership, and any failure triggers an automatic slash of the bonded stake. The attacker must acquire and physically control enough distinct enclaves to cover the total bonded value, making a Sybil campaign cost proportional to real hardware and capital.
